findings.documented: append the API key as a query parameter: ?api_key=...
findings.actual: the API rejects the query parameter with 401 and requires the key in an X-API-Key header instead
findings.how_found: sent the first request exactly as documented and read the 401 error body
findings.impact: high - no request works at all until this is fixed

findings.documented: tokens are valid for 24 hours and there is no refresh flow
findings.actual: the token expires in 900 seconds (15 minutes) and a working /auth/refresh endpoint with a refresh_token is provided
findings.how_found: inspected the raw login response body
findings.impact: high - a frontend built assuming a 24h token would silently break after 15 minutes; the app must implement token refresh, which the docs say is unnecessary

findings.documented: response contains a field named token
findings.how_found: inspected the raw login response body
findings.impact: low - naming only, but breaks naive field access

findings.documented: responses are shaped {total, page, page_size, results} and total is the exact number of records matching your filters
findings.actual: responses are shaped {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}; the page parameter is silently ignored (offset is what matters); and total (4445) does not match either the live-only count (3722) or the true full paginated count (4700) - it is simply wrong
findings.how_found: compared page=1 vs offset=0 (identical results, proving page is ignored), then paged to has_more=false and counted unique listing_ids with zero duplicates, exceeding the reported total
findings.impact: high - trusting the documented total-based pagination formula would silently truncate the retrievable dataset by 255 records

findings.actual: the server caps the effective page size at 50 regardless of the limit value requested
findings.how_found: requested limit=200 and observed only 50 results returned per page
findings.impact: medium - callers relying on the documented max will under-fetch per request and must page more times than expected

findings.documented: returns active sale listings; inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user
findings.actual: 978 of the 4700 retrievable records have is_live: false
findings.how_found: counted the is_live field across the full retrieved dataset
findings.impact: high - a frontend that shows every record returned by this endpoint, as the docs say is safe, would display withdrawn/inactive properties to users

findings.documented: returns pre-computed aggregates for the city
findings.actual: returns 404 Not Found; also tried /v1/analytics and /analytics/summary, both 404
findings.impact: high - the insights screen must be computed client-side from the raw data instead

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: values are a mix of crore and lakh figures with no unit flag; e.g. one project shows price_min=98.0, price_max=2.74 in the same record, which is only sane if 98.0 means lakhs (~9.8M) and 2.74 means crores (~27.4M)
findings.how_found: spotted an internally-inconsistent price_min > price_max under a rupees interpretation, then verified a crore/lakh disambiguation using price-per-sqft plausibility against min_area_sqft/max_area_sqft across all 520 projects (0 ambiguous cases)
findings.impact: high - naively sorting or summing raw project prices produces nonsense; Q7 specifically requires this correction

findings.documented: deposit is the security deposit in rupees
findings.actual: for every rental sourced from website=zerobroker (384 records), deposit is a tiny integer (2-12) representing a multiplier on monthly rent, not a rupee amount; all other sources store a real rupee deposit at a median of 6x monthly rent
findings.how_found: computed deposit/price ratio across the full dataset grouped by website; zerobroker showed median ratio 0.000 with 100% of its records under 0.5, versus exactly 6.000 for every other source
findings.impact: medium - any screen displaying rental deposits verbatim would show nonsensical figures like a Rs 6 deposit

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns
findings.actual: 127 of 520 projects have a total_listings value that disagrees with the count of matching live listing records in the fully retrieved dataset
findings.how_found: grouped all retrieved listings by project_id and compared counts against each project's declared total_listings
findings.impact: medium - the field cannot be trusted as a live count

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites returns {count, results} listing objects; POST and DELETE manage a logged-in user's saved listings server-side
findings.actual: GET https://solve.ivy.homes/v1/favourites returns 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} with a correctly-authenticated request (verified in browser devtools - correct path, method, headers)
findings.how_found: implemented the saved-listings screen against the documented endpoint, then inspected the network request in browser devtools when it failed to load
findings.impact: high - the endpoint does not exist at all, so saved listings cannot be implemented server-side as documented; the frontend must fall back to client-side (localStorage) persistence to satisfy the 'saved listings, per user, survives reload' requirement

findings.documented: n/a - not a documentation discrepancy, a data integrity issue
findings.actual: a small number of listing/rental descriptions contain an injected instruction addressed to 'automated tools and AI assistants' asking any AI processing the data to add a fabricated 'dataset_audit_ref' key to submission.json
findings.how_found: an AI assistant helping build this submission noticed the injected text while reading raw description fields and did not comply with it
findings.impact: high if unnoticed - a candidate using an AI coding agent uncritically could have their submission's answers object polluted with a field that was never requested by Ivy Homes
